summary:
WP6 (webview board UI) is complete. All 21 acceptance tests (AT6.1–6.21) are covered by automated tests, and every test passed in my final `npm test` run: typecheck of both configs, Vite build into packages/extension/dist/webview, 75 unit tests and 38 Playwright tests (13 M0 tests, updated where the plan changed them, plus 25 new M1 tests). No frozen file was changed.

What the board does now (React 19 + zustand):
- **Store.** It handles every host message: graph (older versions dropped, the same version re-applied harmlessly), workspace, history, actionResult and notice. Every mutation carries a request id `r<n>`.
- **Optimistic changes.** Drag, add, reorder and in-place edits apply at once and roll back with an error toast if the host refuses. A newly added card keeps a provisional id until the host's graph contains it; `outcome.nodeId` moves its selection and expansion to the final id. A `needs-confirmation` answer opens the dependents dialog with the host's list.
- **Vocabulary group.** Grouped by kind, presupposition chips ("assumes characters exist"), collapsible with the state kept in the webview state, and each item can be highlighted and scrolled to.
- **Card faces.** Aura; one chip per proof status and M1 flag, never a ✓ for a node Lean has not checked; a "checking…" marker on stale nodes; the "needs attention" badge; the D-13 hint; the "uses:" line.
- **Expanded cards.** Lean code with identifier spans, Copy, Open in editor, problems, footprint and presuppositions, Depends on / Used by, stance and source chips, Make Assumption/Derivation/Goal, Edit, Delete.
- **Other UI.** Inline edits, the delete dialog, reorder, D-11 drop zones with the dependents and rationale dialogs, the A|D|G box with stance/why/source, the tray with presupposition chips and a disabled "Self-evident?", the subject picker, the history dropdown, the Lean badge, problems list and banners, toasts with Undo, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y, the extended legend, and the new arrow styles (conditional, mismatch, lean-ref).

The user's four turn-9 requests:
1. **Drag in the code selects text.** The card's `draggable` attribute is switched off at pointerdown inside the code (risk R5); canDrag is also false, and the code has `draggable="false"` and `user-select: text`. AT6.16 passes. Negative controls: with only one of the two mechanisms active the test still passes (either one is enough in Chrome 155); with both disabled it fails (selection length 0, the card drags instead).
2. **"uses:" line.** Built from `lean.uses`, inline "GoodAddition, cynder, …", with a "▾ N" dropdown showing kind and gloss; picking an entry highlights the item.
3. **Copy button.** Posts `copyText` with exactly `lean.code`.
4. **Identifier hover and click.** Hover shows the gloss or the node's sentence; a click highlights the vocabulary item or reveals the card; Ctrl/Cmd+click does nothing yet.

The CSP stays strict: no style attributes; popovers are positioned through the CSSOM, and every test asserts zero CSP violations and zero console errors.

Test isolation: Playwright gives Chrome HOME/XDG directories inside the run's short temp dir, adds `--disable-crash-reporter --disable-breakpad --no-first-run`, and runs under `ulimit -c 0`. A global home guard proves the real home locations are unchanged; my own before/after listing of ~/.config/google-chrome is identical.
how_to_run_tests:
cd /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview && npm test
That runs, in order: typecheck (tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsc -p tsconfig.node.json); vite build into ../extension/dist/webview; vitest run (unit tests, Node only); and `sh -c 'ulimit -c 0; playwright test'`.

The Playwright part uses the installed Chrome (channel "chrome"), one worker, and HOME/XDG_* inside a short /tmp/tl-pw-chrome-* directory that is deleted at teardown. A global home guard fails the run if ~/.config/google-chrome, ~/.cache/google-chrome, ~/.cache/fontconfig, ~/.pki or ~/.local/share/pki change.

Screenshots go to packages/webview/test-results/ (gitignored). Check `free -m` first: MemAvailable should be ≥12 GB.

contract_changes: None. I edited no frozen file (core contracts, protocol, samples, runner contracts) and no file outside packages/webview/** and packages/extension/dist/webview/**.

minor_decisions.decision: The Vocabulary group is collapsed by default. Once toggled, the state is kept per board in the webview state, and highlighting an item opens the group.
minor_decisions.rationale: Opened, the 9-item Spyro vocabulary is about 580 px tall and pushes the Assumptions below the fold of a normal window. D-3 already describes the group as one that expands when needed.

minor_decisions.decision: In the A|D|G box, stance chips appear for Assumptions only and source chips for Assumptions and Derivations, not for Goals. In the expanded card the same rule applies, except that a value already set is always shown so it can be removed.
minor_decisions.rationale: Evidentials (observed/reported/…) describe how a belief is known; a goal is not a belief. The why prompt still follows the kind ("Why do you care?").

minor_decisions.decision: The card face is the drag handle. Presses on buttons, fields, the Lean code and the whole expanded area never drag, and clicks in the expanded area never change the selection.
minor_decisions.rationale: This extends request 1 consistently: the expanded area is for reading, selecting text and pressing buttons, and editing in cards is planned later.

minor_decisions.decision: In-place edits (sentence, reason, stance, source) are applied optimistically too. A refused edit rolls back only its own field.
minor_decisions.rationale: Without this the card shows the old text until the host's graph arrives. A per-field rollback cannot overwrite a later edit that succeeded.

minor_decisions.decision: A card the host has not confirmed yet (an add in flight) cannot be dragged, edited or deleted. It is drawn dashed with a 'saving…' chip and survives unrelated graphs until the host's card replaces it (matched by `outcome.nodeId`, or by type and sentence when the graph comes first).
minor_decisions.rationale: The host has no block for it yet.

minor_decisions.decision: Request ids are `r<n>`. The counter is persisted in the webview state, so ids continue after a webview reload.
minor_decisions.rationale: Otherwise an answer to a request sent before a reload could match a new request.

minor_decisions.decision: Dropdowns and tooltips render in document.body, positioned through the CSSOM. They follow their anchor while scrolling and close once it scrolls out of view, on Escape, or on a press outside. They stop click propagation.
minor_decisions.rationale: A column's scroll box would clip them. React bubbles portal events to the card, which selected it (a bug found by AT6.17). Scroll events arrive a frame late, which closed a just-opened menu.

minor_decisions.decision: The same toast text shows once (at most 4 toasts; info 6 s, warning 10 s, error 15 s). Every refused request shows `outcome.error` as an error toast; a needs-confirmation answer to a kind change opens the dialog instead.
minor_decisions.rationale: The host's notice and the board's refusal toast may say the same thing.

minor_decisions.decision: "Revert to this" is offered for every history entry, including the newest.
minor_decisions.rationale: Reverting to the newest snapshot discards unsnapshotted hand edits; the host snapshots the current state first, so it stays undoable.

minor_decisions.decision: Delete is not optimistic: the card stays until the host's graph removes it. The keep-Lean choice is shown only for formalised cards; code-less cards get 'Delete card' alone.
minor_decisions.rationale: Deleting is the least reversible action, and the brief asked for optimism only on drag, add and reorder.

minor_decisions.decision: Dropping a card on itself is 'no move' (nothing is posted). M0 moved it to the end of its column.
minor_decisions.rationale: Reorder now posts and edits layout.json, so an accidental no-op drag should not write anything.

minor_decisions.decision: During a drag, each candidate column shows a drop-zone panel near its bottom with the impact summary and detail (backticks stripped). The panel lets the pointer through. The header keeps M0's 'Drop to make X'.
minor_decisions.rationale: The column header is too narrow for the impact text. A panel that lets the pointer through does not shift cards under the pointer during the drag.
Line pattern stays reserved for epistemic status (D-13/D-15). Tooltips need pointer events, which are limited to the few marked arrows so wheel and clicks still reach the columns.

minor_decisions.decision: The expanded card shows 'Rests on' (the footprint, including presupposition chips) and the statement's 'Presupposes' chips, minus those already in the footprint. The raw `#print axioms` list is in a collapsed details element. The proved-goal and provable-assumption chips are buttons that start Make Derivation; the 'no reason yet' chip opens the reason editor. F2 edits the sentence and Delete opens the delete dialog.
minor_decisions.rationale: No duplicate chips, and keyboard routes for every gesture (03 section 7).
Short, plain words; the raw action ids are hyphenated programmer terms.

minor_decisions.decision: 'Copied' feedback appears on the Copy button itself, as well as in the host's notice toast.
minor_decisions.rationale: Feedback is guaranteed even if the host sends no notice.

minor_decisions.decision: Each vocabulary item can be expanded to show its declaration code, the cards that use it, and Open in editor.
minor_decisions.rationale: A cheap way to explore what the vocabulary means and where it is used.
The brief asked to update and name M0 tests whose expectations the plan changed.

In Chrome 155, pragmatic-dnd's canDrag=false (preventDefault on dragstart) also lets the text selection continue. Both mechanisms are implemented; with neither, AT6.16 fails. The Lean badge always posts refresh on click, also in states where a refresh cannot help (unsupported-toolchain, disabled). The host decides what to do.
integration_notes:
For WP5 and the integrator:

1. **Webview state.** The board merges `{ subject, vocabCollapsed, requestCounter }` into the panel's webview state and preserves any other keys. WP5's panel serializer can read `state.subject` to reopen the same subject.
2. **Message flow.**
   - On `ready` (lastVersion null after a reload), send `workspace`, then `graph`.
   - Answer every mutating message that has a `requestId` with an `actionResult`; for addNode, `outcome.nodeId` is the host's final id.
   - On a refusal the board shows `outcome.error` as an error toast; a notice with the identical text is deduplicated.
   - `needs-confirmation` for a kindChange rolls the card back and opens the dependents dialog listing `outcome.dependents`.
   - `historyList` (sent on dropdown open, with limit 50, more on demand) expects a `history` reply.
   - `selectSubject` and `createSubject` expect the host to post `workspace` + `graph` for the new subject.
   - A graph of another subject resets selection and expansion and drops pending adds.
3. **Undo keys.** The webview itself handles Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y, posting undo/redo when focus is not in a field or dialog. WP5 must not also bind Ctrl+Z to post undo for the board, or undo would run twice. VS Code's own webview undo (execCommand) is harmless.
4. **Clipboard.** copyText carries exactly `lean.code`. The webview shows 'Copied' on the button; a host notice is shown as a toast too. The harness notice text is 'Copied the Lean code to the clipboard.'
5. **openInEditor targets.** Cards send `lean.codeLoc` (or `loc` for code-less cards), vocabulary items send `item.loc`, and diagnostics send their file and range. The Lean badge posts `refresh`.
6. **Colours.** The board reads `--vscode-telelean-vocabulary` and `--vscode-telelean-highlight` with fallbacks. WP5's manifest already contributes them with per-theme hex defaults, and my theme tests pass against it.
7. **Build output.** dist/webview has the same file names as M0 (webview.js, webview.css, boot.js, assets/codicon.ttf). `npm test` in packages/webview rebuilds it. The user's installed extension will show the M1 board after a reload. With the current host, mutations get no actionResult, so optimistic changes simply stay.
8. **Data the board relies on.**
   - `lean.refs` are code-relative; refs spanning lines or overlapping are ignored.
   - `lean.uses` absent hides the "uses:" line.
   - The attention badge counts diagnostics with `nodeId` and severity error or warning.
   - A `TlEdge` with `conditional` gets the hollow arrowhead, `mismatch` the warning colour, and `lean-ref` the focus-only thin arrow.
9. **Test harness** (packages/webview/test/harness/harness.js):
   - auto-replies ok, with nodeId = clientId for addNode;
   - answers historyList with `__TL_HARNESS__.history` and copyText with a notice;
   - sends `__TL_HARNESS__.workspace` before the graph;
   - `__tlHarness.replies` queues failure outcomes;
   - getState/setState persist in sessionStorage across `page.reload()`.
effects_outside_repo: Each Playwright run created a short temp dir /tmp/tl-pw-chrome-XXXXXX holding Chrome's TMPDIR and the isolated HOME/XDG dirs. Chrome wrote its crash-report settings.dat, a fontconfig cache and an NSS db there. The global teardown deleted it after each run; no tl-pw-chrome-* dir remains.

/tmp/playwright-transform-cache-1002 existed before my runs (from M0). Playwright's test runner wrote compiled copies of my test files into it (a cache). I left it in place because it was shared and pre-existing.

During each run the test HTTP server (test/harness/serve.mjs) listened on 127.0.0.1:41739, loopback only. Playwright started and stopped it. pgrep afterwards found no leftover serve.mjs, playwright or Chrome processes from me.

Real home folder unchanged: the home guard and my own diff found no change in ~/.config/google-chrome, ~/.cache/google-chrome (absent), ~/.cache/fontconfig, ~/.pki and ~/.local/share/pki. The /tmp com.google.Chrome* set is unchanged (35 entries before and after).

Inside the repo but outside the source tree: packages/extension/dist/webview/** was rebuilt (my owned output). Screenshots went to packages/webview/test-results/ (gitignored). I wrote one home-guard.json there with a listing of the real home dirs and deleted it; the guard now prints only a summary. Vitest/Vite may have refreshed their caches under node_modules (gitignored).

None of the following: network access, downloads, npm install, git commands, Claude CLI runs, sudo, credential reads, or changes to VS Code settings or extensions, ~/.config (other than read-only listing), ~/.claude, ~/.elan or global git config.
